name: GK Energy Ltd
title: GK Energy Ltd - 544525 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: GK Energy Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 71.1% YoY to INR 505 crore, with PAT up 61.6% to INR 59.7 crore.
summary.overview: GK Energy reported its highest-ever quarterly revenue, with standalone revenue of INR 505 crore (up 71.1% YoY), EBITDA of INR 86.1 crore (margin 17.05%, up 47.7%) and PAT of INR 59.7 crore (up 61.6%). Order book stood at INR 541 crore as of June/early August 2026, including orders received after June. Installations more than doubled to 24,118 systems, and 109 MW of renewable capacity was commissioned, taking the cumulative base to over 164,500 systems and 726 MW. Management reiterated FY27 revenue doubling and PAT in double digits, with the PM-KUSUM 2.0 tender expected in Q3 as the key dependency.

Lower than the 19-20% historical range cited by an analyst; management did not quantify the change
+61.6% YoY vs INR 36.9 crore in Q1 FY26

segments.name: Solar pumps
segments.commentary: About 95% of current revenue and about 80% of the order book, per management. Realisation per pump fell YoY while volumes grew close to double.

segments.name: Rooftop solar
segments.commentary: Newly started; about 5% of current revenue and about 20% of the order book. Management expects it to scale and to be used to offset any PM-KUSUM 2.0 delay.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue doubling target reiterated as 'definitely on that track'; an analyst cited a roughly INR 3,000 crore revenue target, which management did not dispute.
Q1 typically 15-20% of annual volume; Q4 typically 35-40%, so H2 is expected to carry the bulk of the year.
PAT expected to stay at the Q1 run-rate (double-digit PAT margin/level) for the full year, per management.
Realisation per pump expected to stay flat unless PM-KUSUM 2.0 specifications change.
Interest expense expected to stay near the current INR 5 crore level, as IPO proceeds fund working capital and no bank debt is drawn.
Long-term vision of a USD 1 billion revenue enterprise by 2030, with a product mix beyond solar pumps (BESS and hybrid solutions under consideration).
capex_capacity: Business model remains low-capex, relying on OEM/ODM manufacturing partners; management sees no need for backward integration at present, citing existing manufacturer capacity in the market.
Decentralised warehousing, logistics and field network of 1,500+ staff, 40+ owned vehicles, covering more than 7,500 villages.
No specific capex amount or new capacity commissioning timeline was disclosed.
demand_pricing: Management expects PM-KUSUM 2.0 tender/scheme to come in Q3 FY27 and expects work to start by end-Q3; the analyst's question on a possible delay was answered only with 'slight impact' and a pivot to rooftop.
Magel Tyala Phase 6 bid recently submitted; Phase 7 in pipeline.
Realisation per pump fell YoY as volumes grew; management expects flat realisation unless specifications change in PM-KUSUM 2.0.
Management stated that PM-KUSUM 1.0 volume should be multiplied several times in 2.0; it referred to Maharashtra as about 70% of national solar pump business.
Competition was acknowledged as a factor in lower per-pump realisation, but no competitor was named.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR 541 crore order book enough for doubling FY27 revenue, and is margin compression expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is confident of the doubling track, with Magel Tyala Phase 6/7 and PM-KUSUM 2.0 and rooftop as drivers. It guided PAT to stay at the Q1 level for the full year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status and timing of PM-KUSUM 2.0?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q3 FY27 is the expected timing and that work should start by end-Q3. It said the press release on subsumed funds related to a legislative-assembly answer, not PM-KUSUM 2.0.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company reach about INR 3,000 crore revenue in the remaining three quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 is usually 15-20% of annual volume and Q4 35-40%, so the back-end-loaded pattern supports the target. It said growth would be 'slightly plus/minus' the Q1 rate.

qa_highlights.question: Why did realisation per pump fall while volumes doubled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed lower realisation per pump but higher total volume. It expects realisation to stay flat unless PM-KUSUM 2.0 specifications change.

qa_highlights.question: Is backward integration planned as part of the USD 1 billion by 2030 vision?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is not clear on backward integration, since manufacturing capacity already exists in the market. It said further product additions are under consideration and PM-KUSUM is one of several drivers.

qa_highlights.question: Why did interest expense fall from INR 11 crore to INR 5 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited surplus cash from strong receivables in FY26 and IPO proceeds used for working capital, with no bank debt. It said the INR 5 crore level will persist.

risks_watch: PM-KUSUM 2.0 timing: management expects Q3 FY27, but no official tender date was given; a delay would hit H2 volumes, which carry most of the year.
Margin pressure: EBITDA margin of 17.05% is below the 19-20% level an analyst referenced, and per-pump realisation is falling as competition grows.
Order book of INR 541 crore covers only part of the INR 1,000+ crore run-rate implied by doubling FY27 revenue (FY26 base not stated in the call), so order inflows must accelerate.
Rooftop is still about 5% of revenue, so it cannot yet offset a large PM-KUSUM shortfall.
Management answers on the PM-KUSUM timeline and realisations were largely qualitative ('as a businessman, we remain positive'), with no firm numbers provided.
summary.management_tone: Confident on near-term delivery and on the FY27 targets, but evasive on the PM-KUSUM 2.0 timeline and on realisation trends, which management kept qualitative. Repeated answers relied on 'Q3' and 'we are on track' without new data.
key_quotes: We have started FY2027 on a positive note, delivering our highest ever quarterly revenue.
So, quarter four goes around 35% to 40% of the business in some of the years.
We are definitely on that track only.

growth.why: Management reiterated FY27 revenue doubling ("definitely on that track") and PAT held at Q1 run-rate, backed by a INR 541 crore order book (80% solar pumps, 20% rooftop) and PM-KUSUM 2.0 tender expected in Q3, but no company-owned capacity additions or capex were disclosed and the key tender timing is a dependency.
